subject: Phased commit smoothing and term discount approval
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novus.ai>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: ops@novus.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-year prepay proposal + phased ramp questions

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week — Novus is excited about Redwood's latency profile for embedding and streaming generations. We ran a quick internal model of our expected usage and are interested in a 3-year prepay to lock unit economics, but there are two asks we want to discuss before moving to procurement:

1) Phased ramp / smoothing: our usage will be seasonal with a heavy ramp in months 7–12 (year 2). We were hoping to structure year 1 payments at 50% of committed ARR, year 2 at 100%, year 3 at 150% (i.e., phased percentage of the total committed tokens) to match our cash flow.
2) Term discount: given the 3-year term and the front/back-loaded usage variance, we need a meaningful blended discount versus standard list — target ~28% off list over the term, with true-up flexibility for overrun months.

I've attached a draft MAP and a simple spreadsheet with our proposed billing cadence. Can Redwood provide guidance on acceptable ramp smoothing and whether a blended discount at that level is possible (and any finance prerequisites)?

Appreciate a quick read — procurement wants an initial commercial term sheet by EOD Friday.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform Ops, Novus AI
ops@novus.ai

Attachments: novus_proposal_Q1-Q3-3yr.xlsx, mutual_action_plan_v2.docx
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novus.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-year prepay proposal + phased ramp questions

Hi Samantha — great to hear from you, and glad the demo resonated.

Short answers up front: we can absolutely support a phased payment schedule and a blended discount for a 3-year commit; there are a couple of finance guardrails we'll need to confirm (true-up mechanics and an initial minimum for year 1 to cover provisioning).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll run your proposed cadence and volumes against our pricing model and draft a blended discount proposal.
- Loop in Revenue Ops (Kimberly) for approval on the discount band and any billing cadence constraints.
- If OK, we can provide a preliminary term sheet and a doc with the true-up process.

Can you confirm the token/embedding split in the attached spreadsheet (there are some blank rows on page 2)? If you can resend a cleaned file I’ll prioritize this.

I’ll aim to get a draft term sheet to you by Wednesday EOD.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novus.ai>

Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-year prepay proposal + phased ramp questions

Thanks Connor — uploaded the cleaned spreadsheet here and clarified the embedding/token mix (70% embeddings, 30% generation).

A couple of clarifications:
- The year 1 50% figure is a cash-flow imperative for us; we can stretch a small minimum true-up but need the invoice schedule to reflect the smoothing.
- On discounts: procurement is clear that without a material blended rate the CFO won't sign off. 28% is our ask; we expect to do a joint case study if the partnership lands.

Link to updated sheet: https://drive.novus/cleaned_proposal_v2.xlsx

Let us know if you need more detail.

—Samantha
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novus.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-year prepay proposal + phased ramp questions

Connor / Samantha — looping in Revenue Ops to confirm acceptable discount and billing constraints. Quick notes from my side after a fast model:

- We can support a phased invoicing cadence (50% / 100% / 150% of baseline committed units by year) provided there is a contractual minimum for year 1 equal to 40% of the nominal committed ARR (this protects provisioning while giving you smoothing).
- Blended discount: for a 3-year, $1.8M committed-net (net of discounts) profile with standard risk mitigations and a single contract signature, we can offer a 24% blended discount off list if Novus agrees to the year-1 minimum above and a quarterly true-up (30-day invoice lag).
- If Novus can accelerate to a 50% upfront payment for the first invoice (vs. purely invoiced), we can move to 26%. A CFO-signed LOI or SOW helps us trigger the deeper band.

Attachments: revenue_ops_pricing_note.pdf

If that structure looks acceptable to you, Connor — please prepare a redlineable term sheet. Samantha — if you can confirm that the year 1 minimum of 40% and quarterly true-up are workable, we can lock pricing and get legal working on the SOW.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novus.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-year prepay proposal + phased ramp questions

Samantha — good news. Kimberly's counter is below in plain language: 24% blended discount with a contractual year-1 minimum at 40% of nominal committed ARR and quarterly true-ups (30-day lag). If Novus can do a 50% upfront for the first invoice or provide a signed LOI, we can increase to 26%.

Can you confirm today whether the 40% minimum and quarterly true-ups are acceptable, and whether Novus can do the 50% upfront step (or provide an LOI)? If yes, I'll produce a term sheet and route to legal.

If you'd like, I'm happy to jump on a 30-minute call this afternoon to walk through the invoice cadence and true-up examples.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this with you.
